claims.subject: Money-critical guard path: idle-stop clamp (F-5)
claims.why: The original asked for the money-critical paths to be hardened with tests, but `_idle_minutes_since_boot`/`decide` still compare the provider's per-GPU idle seconds against the idle window without clamping to uptime, so a 32-second-old paid pod can be stopped, and no test in tests/ covers it, while CHARTER.md marks R3 'met'.

claims.subject: MCP `rentguard_run` command handling
claims.why: `dispatch` passes `command.split()` to `cmd_run`, so `_remote_command` shell-quotes each word and a compound or quoted command (`a; b`, `>`, `-c 'print(1)'`) is mangled; the MCP run tool does not mean what CLI `run` means, and this is the same defect M2 run 1 found and fixed only on the CLI.

claims.subject: Documentation of `up --dry-run` (F-4)
claims.why: limitations.md, cap.md, quickstart.md, VERIFICATION.md and KNOWN-FAILURES.md all say `--dry-run` calls create and has no test, but cli.py checks `dry_run` before the create loop and tests/test_money_paths.py::DryRunSpendsNothing covers it, so the docs describe a different tool from the one in the tree.

claims.subject: Open-defect register
claims.why: F-1 (state id erased on 404) and F-3 (fixed default instance name) are still listed as open, but `cli._pod` no longer clears the id, `_instance_name` now derives from the project root, and tests/test_known_failures.py and InstanceNaming cover both, which breaks the file's own rule that a defect leaves when a test covers it.

claims.subject: Quickstart configuration guidance
claims.why: It says the generated file writes `volume_name` (cli.py `_template` writes `volume_id`, and tests/test_init_config.py asserts that), and its sample TOML puts `state_dir` below `[runpod]`, the exact placement README.md says gets silently swallowed into the table.

claims.subject: M2 pass criterion 6 ('closing total under $2')
claims.why: The criterion is stated as the ledger's closing total being under $2, but the same page records $2.15 against the cap and marks the criterion passed by substituting the $0.017 sum of the two runs.

claims.subject: Real-GPU end-to-end proof record (charter R5/R4)
claims.why: R5 claims '3 rentals, $0.0264' reconciled by hand, while docs/M2-REAL-RENTAL.md, CHANGELOG.md and docs/VERIFICATION.md record two rentals for $0.017; also R4 says watch never ran on a rented pod while W4 says a paid run's guard stopped a 32-second-old pod, so the proof the original asked for is recorded inconsistently.

claims.subject: Release-readiness status
claims.why: The status table says nothing remains before the publication question (and cites 58 tests), while CHARTER.md lists R2, R4 and R10 as NOT MET, the guard defect is open, and pyproject.toml deliberately omits the project URLs the checklist itself requires, so 'publishable' has been redefined downward.

claims.subject: CHANGELOG MCP claim
claims.why: It says the MCP server lets agents 'rent, watch and stop machines', but mcp_server.py exposes no watch tool and docs/mcp.md states watch is not exposed.

claims.subject: Coverage target R10 (94% code / 100% features) with ratchet tooling
claims.why: The frozen original sets no coverage target, yet tools/coverage.py, .github/workflows/ci.yml and CHARTER.md attribute a 94%/100% target to 'the user' and gate CI on a ratchet floor.

claims.subject: Tracked probe scripts and run transcripts in the release tree
claims.why: tests/_artefacts/ ships two probe scripts and seven UTF-16 PowerShell transcripts. They contain the local user path C:\Users\besen\..., German shell error noise and stale FAILED runs, and nothing in the original asked for them in a publishable release.

claims.subject: Widening the no-publish rule to every project (W2 scope 'all')
claims.why: The original's no-publish instruction concerns this rentguard release; the charter's Scopes section extends it into a rule for all projects.

claims.subject: ssh known-hosts handling vs limitations doc
claims.why: `ssh_argv` hard-codes `UserKnownHostsFile=NUL` on every OS. cli.py `_ssh` only substitutes a `{null}` placeholder that is never present, so Linux and macOS get a file named NUL, while docs/limitations.md says NUL is used on Windows.

claims.subject: Fake-provider demonstration transcript
claims.why: The 'real output' shown includes lines (healthy, crash_loop, disappear, idle decision) that the printed script cannot produce, so the transcript does not belong to the code beside it.
